current_bottleneck: 492a showed that separately learned conditional marginal quantiles on top of the strong 392a rank/path sampler are not path-law neutral: they slightly improve aggregate coverage but damage daily-change, level occupancy, mean-reversion, cointegration, and pathwise jump diagnostics.
last_result_summary: 492a trained a lightweight conditional quantile marginal model and used frozen 392a samples only for samplewise ranks. It scored 3/11, passing only surface, block_ar, and cross-cell correlation. Versus 392a, level KS fell 10/25 -> 1/25, daily KS 25/25 -> 16/25, mean-reversion ratio 1.024 -> 1.362, pathwise KS 0.373 -> 0.551, and per-cell q99 pass 22/25 -> 10/25.
next_step_recommendation: Do not salvage 492a with extra marginal knobs. Return to the 392a frontier and choose a path-law-preserving intervention for the three remaining failures, or run a post-experiment analysis if that intervention is not yet clean enough to state in one sentence.
current_best_note: Ties the official revised-suite 8/11 frontier with better residual geometry than 385a: level KS 10/25, median-bias fraction 20/25, bias magnitude 25/25, daily KS 25/25, conditionality pass, and cointegration pass. Architecture is unchanged; the change is a theoretically proper free-running path-energy score fine-tune anchored by FM.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
